econ-fin-01-c4.text: Ivo Welch (2022). Stock and Bond Valuation: Annuities and Perpetuities (Corporate Finance, ch. 3). Corporate Finance (textbook chapter, corpfin.ivo-welch.org).
econ-fin-01-c4.quote: The growing perpetuity formula allows for a constant rate g per period, provided it is less than the interest rate.
econ-fin-01-c4.claim: A growing perpetuity pays C, then C(1+g), then C(1+g)², forever. Its PV = C/(r-g), provided r > g.

econ-fin-01-c4.text: Ivo Welch (2022). Stock and Bond Valuation: Annuities and Perpetuities (Corporate Finance, ch. 3). Corporate Finance (textbook chapter, corpfin.ivo-welch.org).
econ-fin-01-c4.quote: In this context, the growing perpetuity model is often called the Gordon growth model, after its inventor, Myron Gordon.
econ-fin-01-c4.claim: That's the Gordon growth model, used to price stocks under the assumption of steady dividend growth.

econ-fin-01-c5.text: Campbell R. Harvey and Stephen Gray (1997). Valuation of Cash Flows II: Investment Decisions and Capital Budgeting. Duke University Fuqua School of Business, WWWFinance Global Financial Management.
econ-fin-01-c5.quote: Accept a project if its NPV > 0;
econ-fin-01-c5.claim: The investment decision rule built on present value is short: invest if and only if NPV > 0.

econ-fin-02-c4.text: (1990). Press release: The Prize in Economic Sciences 1990. NobelPrize.org.
econ-fin-02-c4.quote: Hence, the essential aspect pertaining to the risk of an asset is not the risk of each asset in isolation, but the contribution of each asset to the risk of the aggregate portfolio.
econ-fin-02-c4.claim: The fundamental insight is that an asset's contribution to portfolio risk is not its standalone variance, it's its covariance with the rest of the portfolio.

econ-fin-02-c5.text: (2013). Popular science background: The Prize in Economic Sciences 2013. NobelPrize.org.
econ-fin-02-c5.quote: Risky assets are less attractive to investors, so on average, a risky asset will need to deliver a higher return.
econ-fin-02-c5.claim: Risk premia exist because investors are risk-averse and demand extra return to hold risky assets.

econ-fin-03-c2.text: (1990). Press release: The Prize in Economic Sciences 1990. NobelPrize.org.
econ-fin-03-c2.quote: However, the “law of large numbers” is not wholly applicable to the diversification of risks in portfolio choice because the returns on different assets are correlated in practice. Thus, in general, risk cannot be totally eliminated, regardless of how many types of securities are represented in a portfolio.
econ-fin-03-c2.claim: Systematic (market) risk: affects all assets, can't be diversified away.

econ-fin-03-c3.text: (1990). Press release: The Prize in Economic Sciences 1990. NobelPrize.org.
econ-fin-03-c3.quote: The contribution for which Harry Markowitz now receives his award was first published in an essay entitled “Portfolio Selection” (1952), and later, more extensively, in his book, Portfolio Selection: Efficient Diversification (1959).
econ-fin-03-c3.claim: Markowitz (1952) formalized the choice problem: given a set of assets, what portfolios are 'efficient'?

econ-fin-03-c5.text: (1990). Press release: The Prize in Economic Sciences 1990. NobelPrize.org.
econ-fin-03-c5.quote: Harry Markowitz is awarded the Prize for having developed the theory of portfolio choice; William Sharpe, for his contributions to the theory of price formation for financial assets, the so-called, Capital Asset Pricing Model (CAPM)
econ-fin-03-c5.claim: Markowitz's framework won a Nobel in 1990.

econ-fin-04-c1.text: (1990). Press release: The Prize in Economic Sciences 1990. NobelPrize.org.
econ-fin-04-c1.quote: According to the CAPM, in an efficient capital market, the risk premium and thus also the expected return on an asset, will vary in direct proportion to the beta value.
econ-fin-04-c1.claim: The Capital Asset Pricing Model (Sharpe 1964, Lintner 1965, Mossin 1966): in equilibrium, an asset's expected return equals the risk-free rate plus a premium proportional to its systematic risk.

econ-fin-04-c1.text: (1990). Press release: The Prize in Economic Sciences 1990. NobelPrize.org.
econ-fin-04-c1.quote: Shares with a beta coefficient greater than 1 have an above-average effect on the risk of the aggregate portfolio, whereas shares with a beta coefficient of less than 1 have a lower than average effect on the risk of the aggregate portfolio.
econ-fin-04-c1.claim: β > 1 means it amplifies market moves; β < 1 means it dampens them.

econ-fin-04-c4.text: (2013). Popular science background: The Prize in Economic Sciences 2013. NobelPrize.org.
econ-fin-04-c4.quote: Just as a low general valuation of stocks in relation to dividends predicts high future returns, so-called value stocks (with a high book-to-market ratio) tend to yield high returns relative to stocks with a low book-to-market value.
econ-fin-04-c4.claim: Value (HML): high book-to-market (value) stocks earn higher returns than low book-to-market (growth) stocks.

econ-fin-05-c1.text: (2013). Popular science background: The Prize in Economic Sciences 2013. NobelPrize.org.
econ-fin-05-c1.quote: Then they would buy the stock immediately, driving up the price until it is so high that the stock is no longer attractive to buy. What remains is an unpredictable price pattern, with random movements that reflect the arrival of news.
econ-fin-05-c1.claim: The intuition: if a profitable trade was obvious, smart investors would already have made it, pushing prices to where the trade is no longer profitable.

econ-fin-05-c3.text: (2013). Press release: The Prize in Economic Sciences 2013. NobelPrize.org.
econ-fin-05-c3.quote: There is no way to predict the price of stocks and bonds over the next few days or weeks. But it is quite possible to foresee the broad course of these prices over longer periods, such as the next three to five years.
econ-fin-05-c3.claim: The empirical record: short-horizon (daily, weekly) returns are very close to random walks.

econ-fin-05-c5.text: Andrei Shleifer, Robert W. Vishny (1995). The Limits of Arbitrage. NBER Working Paper 5167.
econ-fin-05-c5.quote: Such professional arbitrage has a number of interesting implications for security pricing, including the possibility that arbitrage becomes ineffective in extreme circumstances, when prices diverge far from fundamental values.
econ-fin-05-c5.claim: Limits to arbitrage (Shleifer-Vishny): real arbitrage is risky and capital-constrained.

econ-fin-06-c1.text: (1997). Press release: The Prize in Economic Sciences 1997. NobelPrize.org.
econ-fin-06-c1.quote: Due to their design, options allow for hedging against one-sided risk – options give the right, but not the obligation, to buy or sell a certain security in the future at a prespecified price.
econ-fin-06-c1.claim: Options: the right (not obligation) to buy or sell at a fixed price.

econ-fin-06-c3.text: (1997). Press release: The Prize in Economic Sciences 1997. NobelPrize.org.
econ-fin-06-c3.quote: Consider a so-called European call option that gives the right to buy one share in a certain firm at a strike price of $ 50, three months from now.
econ-fin-06-c3.claim: Call option: right to buy at strike K.

econ-fin-06-c4.text: (1997). Press release: The Prize in Economic Sciences 1997. NobelPrize.org.
econ-fin-06-c4.quote: This year’s laureates, Robert Merton and Myron Scholes, developed this method in close collaboration with Fischer Black, who died in his mid-fifties in 1995. These three scholars worked on the same problem: option valuation.
econ-fin-06-c4.claim: Fischer Black, Myron Scholes, and Robert Merton's 1973 result earned a Nobel Prize (Scholes and Merton; Black had died).

econ-fin-07-c2.text: Jay Ritter, Ivo Welch (2002). A Review of IPO Activity, Pricing, and Allocations. NBER Working Paper 8805.
econ-fin-07-c2.quote: We review the theory and evidence on IPO activity: why firms go public, why they reward first-day investors with considerable underpricing, and how IPOs perform in the long run.
econ-fin-07-c2.claim: The price is typically set just below expected first-day market price: the famous 'IPO underpricing' that gives early investors immediate gains while leaving money on the table for the issuer.

econ-fin-07-c5.text: Donald Bernhardt, Marshall Eckblad. Stock Market Crash of 1987. Federal Reserve History.
econ-fin-07-c5.quote: In the United States, the Dow Jones Industrial Average (DJIA) dropped 22.6 percent in a single trading session, a loss that remains the largest one-day stock market decline in history.
econ-fin-07-c5.claim: Crashes can be sudden (1987's Black Monday lost 22% in a day) or grinding (2000-02 dot-com bust took two years).
